summary: Read-only adversarial pass on retained PR #477 found one distinct unpinned branch worth considering if it fits your generation-3 scope: an incoming duplicate can be individually valid under MAX_CANONICAL_METADATA_STRING_BYTES while the combined returned duplicate diagnostic exceeds MAX_PERSISTENT_STATE_STRING_BYTES, causing retention to be intentionally skipped. Existing retained tests cover invalid over-budget incoming metadata, but not a valid combined-oversize diagnostic or preservation of an already-retained bounded history entry. Production code appears correct; this is a regression-coverage gap, not a source defect claim.
evidence: PR #477 exact head fdd5bbe85f0f813172cb5b1e8564550b9c9beb96 register() first fully owns/validates the incoming record, then computes retainedStringBytes across entityId, kinds, legacy recipe keys, and both complete origins; if that combined evidence exceeds MAX_PERSISTENT_STATE_STRING_BYTES it returns the frozen diagnostic but does not append/evict duplicate history.

tests/world_entity.luau at #477 checks a plainly oversized metadata fixture but allows WorldEntity.new() rejection itself to satisfy bounded-retention proof, so that case cannot reach the valid-record combined-diagnostic retention branch.
tests/world_entity_metadata_budget.luau at #477 explicitly proves an over-budget direct duplicate is rejected before duplicate handling/history, which is a different boundary.

A focused passing fixture can retain one small diagnostic, then submit a same-ID duplicate with recipeKey length just over half the 65536 diagnostic budget while keeping its individual canonical metadata below 65536; expected behavior is duplicate rejection + complete returned diagnostic + prior retained history unchanged + first registration still authoritative.
